caution: A failure to reproduce is not a finding that the paper is wrong. It may be a failure of the attempt.

attempts.label: CRCNS:alm-3
attempts.paper_title: Robust neuronal dynamics in premotor cortex during motor planning
attempts.entry_title: Robust preparatory activity in mouse premotor cortex (Li, Daie, Svoboda and Druckmann 2016)
attempts.summary: Several central findings held up in this data: selectivity along the coding direction recovered after silencing ALM on one side but not both, predicted the upcoming lick, and after callosotomy no longer recovered from ipsilateral silencing. Single neurons regained selectivity on the paper's time course after unilateral silencing, but in a different neuron set, and in the bilateral experiment only under a few analysis readings. Two central claims did not reproduce: the persistent and ramping modes predicted the lick, and the modular integrator built from the matrix printed in the Methods recovered on one trial type only. The behavioural effect of silencing at the go cue could not be tested, as the behaviour-only sessions are not in the dataset.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Li, Daie, Svoboda and Druckmann (2016) on CRCNS data set alm-3, which holds the sorted single units, trial tables, photostimulus types and lick and laser traces of 91 recording sessions from 19 mice performing a delayed response task with transient unilateral or bilateral photoinhibition of the anterior lateral motor cortex, with and without callosotomy. It covers unit counts and selectivity, silencing and recovery of rates and selectivity, behaviour in the recording sessions, and the population analyses along the coding direction.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Li et al. (2016) from CRCNS alm-3

outcomes.statement: 1012 single units were recorded in left ALM during behaviour across 58 sessions (20 unilateral, 38 bilateral) from 12 mice; 72 are fast-spiking, 890 putative pyramidal and 50 of intermediate width are excluded.
outcomes.source: Methods, Electrophysiology data analysis, paragraph 1; Results, Preparatory activity in ALM
outcomes.quote: 1012 single units were recorded during behavior across 58 recording sessions (20 sessions of unilateral experiments, Fig. 1 ; 38 sessions of bilateral experiments ... (FS) neurons (72/1012) and units with spike widths > 0.45 ms as putative pyramidal neurons (890/1012). Units with intermediate values (0.35 - 0.45 ms, 50/1012) were excluded
outcomes.notes: The 58 non-callosotomy sessions (20 unilateral, 38 bilateral) from 12 mice hold 1012 single units, 890 labelled pyramidal, all as the paper reports. 89 units are labelled FS and 33 carry no cell-type label, against 72 FS and 50 intermediate in the paper. By the trough-to-peak width of the deposited mean waveform (29 samples at 19.53 kHz, steps of 0.051 ms) there are 890 pyramidal, 98 FS and 24 intermediate units, and 889, 104 and 19 after tenfold spline upsampling. 15 units labelled FS have a width of 0.358 ms, inside the excluded range. Five of six counts match exactly; the FS count is 24% above the paper's, so neither the criterion's full nor its partial rule holds.
deviations: Cell classes are read from the data set's cellType labels, with the width of the deposited mean waveform as a second reading; the paper's width measurement (interpolation, filtering) is not described beyond trough to peak.

outcomes.statement: Most ALM pyramidal neurons distinguish trial types (634 of 890), 176 during the sample, 337 during the delay and 493 during the response epoch.
outcomes.source: Results, Preparatory activity in ALM; Extended Data Fig. 1b, e
outcomes.quote: Most ALM pyramidal neurons distinguished trial types (634/890, p<0.05, t-test; sample epoch, 176/890; delay epoch, 337/890; response epoch, 493/890, Methods)
outcomes.notes: Correct control trials, lick-early trials excluded, 1.3 s response epoch (reading a of M3 and M1, the code's response window): 633 of 890 pyramidal neurons selective in some epoch, 176 in the sample, 336 in the delay and 493 in the response epoch (paper 634, 176, 337, 493). The 1.5 s response epoch also matches (635 and 490). With correct and error trials, the trials the deposited script selects, the counts are 571, 152, 287 and 404; with lick-early trials included 596, 161, 315 and 433. The first 400 ms after the cue gives 411 response-selective neurons. 1 neuron could not be tested.
deviations: Response epoch taken as the 1.3 s after the cue, from the deposited script (analysis_compile_all_data_unilateral.m, significant selectivity); the 0.4 s and 1.5 s readings of M2 are shown. The authors' MATLAB scripts deposited in the data set (alm-3/live/analyses_scripts/), which the data description says reproduce the paper's figures, are used as the paper's analysis code for details the claims file and the Methods leave open; the paper itself links no code.

outcomes.statement: Unilateral photoinhibition (0.5 s) of ALM ending at the go cue causes an ipsilateral response bias.
outcomes.source: Results, Preparatory activity after unilateral silencing, paragraph 1; Figure 1d
outcomes.quote: Transient (duration, 0.5 s) unilateral photoinhibition of ALM up to the ‘go’ cue (late delay) caused an ipsilateral response bias (n = 5 mice, p < 0.01, two-tailed t-test
outcomes.notes: The recording sessions hold photoinhibition in the sample, early delay and middle delay windows (types 1 to 3, ending 1.6, 0.8 and 0.3 s before the cue by the laser trace); none ends at the go cue. The behaviour-only sessions of Fig. 1d are not in the data set; its FAQ says the published data cover only the electrophysiology sessions. No other public copy was found.

outcomes.statement: Unilateral photoinhibition ending at least 0.3 s before the go cue (early and middle delay) has minimal behavioural effect.
outcomes.source: Results, Preparatory activity after unilateral silencing, paragraph 1; Figure 1d; Extended Data Fig. 3b, d
outcomes.quote: In contrast, photoinhibition ending at least 0.3 s prior to the ‘go’ cue produced minimal behavioral effects (middle delay, early delay; p > 0.1, two-tailed t-test)
outcomes.notes: Recording sessions of Experiment 1, 4 mice (paper 5, behaviour sessions). Performance pooled per mouse: control 79.5%, early delay 74.5% (drop 5.0 points, paired t-test p = 0.23), middle delay 74.9% (drop 4.6, p = 0.22). Unpaired tests and per-session means give p from 0.18 to 0.41. No condition reaches p < 0.05, and all p-values are above the paper's 0.1. Sample photoinhibition +0.6 points (p = 0.81). With four mice the test has little power; the drops are about five points.
deviations: Tested on the recording sessions of Experiment 1 (4 mice, 0.5 s photoinhibition with 100 ms ramp), as the behaviour-only sessions of Fig. 1d are not in the data set; the three sessions with the no-ramp types -1 to -3 are left out, as the data set says not to analyse them.
Performance is hits over hits and errors on performing trials, no-lick and lick-early trials excluded, as the data set's Demo_get_performance.m computes it.

outcomes.statement: Performance is not significantly affected when photoinhibition (0.5 s or 1.3 s) ends more than 0.3 s before the go cue, and 0.5 s of photoinhibition just before the cue has an effect similar to photoinhibition of the whole delay epoch.
outcomes.source: Extended Data Fig. 3b, d, e
outcomes.quote: Performance was not significantly affected for T recovery >0.3s ... Photoinhibition (0.5 s) immediately before the ‘go’ cue is similar to the behavioral effect caused by photoinhibition during the entire delay epoch (1.3 s)
outcomes.notes: Behaviour-only experiments (ED Fig. 3); the data set's FAQ says they are not included, and only types 1 to 3 of ED Fig. 3a are in the recording sessions (see fig1d-earlier-photoinhibition-minimal). The 1.3 s whole-delay photoinhibition and the other recovery intervals are absent. The part on 0.5 s photoinhibition ending 0.8 s and 1.6 s before the cue is tested on the recording sessions under fig1d-earlier-photoinhibition-minimal (p = 0.23 and 0.81, no significant effect); the 1.3 s photoinhibition and the condition ending at the cue are missing, so the claim stays blocked.

outcomes.statement: Photoinhibition silences more than 90% of putative pyramidal activity, similarly with ipsilateral and bilateral photoinhibition and in VGAT-ChR2 and PV x ReaChR mice, while contralateral photoinhibition barely changes the average rate.
outcomes.source: Extended Data Fig. 2b; Methods, Photoinhibition
outcomes.quote: Ipsilateral and bilateral photoinhibition similarly silenced neuronal activity. Average spike rate across the population was little affected by contralateral photoinhibition ... Photoinhibition was similar in the two mouse lines (>90% activity reduction)
outcomes.notes: Window (a), onset to the start of the offset ramp; pyramidal neurons with mean rate of at least 1 spike/s. Reduction (1 minus mean normalized rate): Experiment 1 0.938, 0.931, 0.910; Experiment 2 ipsilateral 0.916 and bilateral 0.924; Experiment 3 ipsilateral 4 spots 0.962 and bilateral 1 spot 0.940; sessions with types 4, 5, 7 0.885 and 0.886. Experiment 2 ipsilateral by line 0.951 (PV x ReaChR, 216 neurons) and 0.845 (VGAT-ChR2, 106). Contralateral mean normalized rate 0.945 (Experiment 2), 1.152 (Experiment 3), 0.986 (types 4, 5, 7). With window (b), the whole period, the Experiment 3 contralateral value is 1.222, outside 0.8 to 1.2, and the VGAT reduction 0.831. The callosotomy sessions, not part of the claim, give 0.880 (ipsilateral) and 0.764 (bilateral). Without the four sessions in which photoinhibition does not lower the rate, the VGAT reduction rises to 0.852 (Experiment 2 ipsilateral) and 0.975 (types 4, 5, 7). Neurons per condition: 180 (Experiment 1), 319 to 323 (Experiment 2), 56 (Experiment 3), against the legend's 117, 110, 109; 300, 294, 301; 52, 52, 102.
deviations: Mouse lines are read from the gene modification in the data set's meta data files.
Neurons need at least 3 photoinhibition and 5 control trials, a standard choice; the paper's n (300, 294, 301 in Experiment 2) are close to the 322, 319, 323 here.

outcomes.statement: The standard photostimulus silences about 90% of spikes in a cortical area of 1 mm radius at half maximum, through all layers.
outcomes.source: Methods, Photoinhibition; Extended Data Fig. 2d
outcomes.quote: The photoinhibition silenced 90% of spikes ( Extended Data Fig. 2b ) in a cortical area of 1mm radius (at half-max) through all cortical layers
outcomes.notes: Measured in 4 untrained mice (ED Fig. 2d); the data set's 19 mice are the behaving electrophysiology and callosotomy mice, and no recordings at varying distance from the light are included.

outcomes.statement: No rebound excitation is seen on average after photoinhibition offset; a small proportion of neurons show rebound, balanced by low-level sustained inhibition in a larger proportion.
outcomes.source: Extended Data Fig. 2c, e; Results, Preparatory activity after unilateral silencing, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: No rebound excitation was detected after photoinhibition offset on average ( d ). A small proportion of neurons showed rebound excitation which was balanced by a low level of sustained inhibition in a larger proportion of neurons
outcomes.notes: Experiment 2, lick right trials, ipsilateral photoinhibition, 306 pyramidal neurons above 1 spike/s. 0 to 400 ms after offset, photoinhibition minus control -0.14 spikes/s (paired t = -0.58, p = 0.565); 400 to 800 ms +0.10 (p = 0.617): no rebound on average. In the first window 24 neurons are significantly excited and 9 suppressed (p < 0.01), the opposite of the balance the criterion requires; without the rate exclusion (408 neurons) 30 and 9; at p < 0.05, 36 and 21. By the sign of the change 125 neurons are higher and 177 lower than control (median -0.28 spikes/s), which fits the paper's "low level of sustained inhibition in a larger proportion". The criterion's second condition fails and it has no partial rule. Whether the count at p < 0.01 reads the paper correctly is asked of a reader (questions/crcns-alm-3.yaml).
deviations: The population test (paired t-test over neurons) is the criterion's standard choice.

outcomes.statement: Within 400 ms after unilateral photoinhibition, spike rates are indistinguishable from control in 90% of neurons; only 10% keep a sustained change.
outcomes.source: Results, Preparatory activity after unilateral silencing, paragraph 2; Figure 1f
outcomes.quote: Within 400 ms after photoinhibition, spike rates became indistinguishable from the unperturbed condition in 90% of the neurons; only 10% of neurons retained a sustained change in spike rate
outcomes.notes: The deposited script's selection (pyramidal, mean rate above 1 spike/s, more than 8 control and more than 3 photoinhibition trials of each type) gives 168, 168 and 175 neurons, as Fig. 1f. Fraction with a significant change: reading (a), window starting at offset, 0.179, 0.196, 0.109 (mean 0.161); reading (b), window centred 400 ms after offset, 0.131, 0.143, 0.091 (mean 0.122). Only the middle delay condition is within 0.1 +- 0.01; all are below 0.2. Without the rate exclusion (224, 225, 241 neurons) reading (b) gives 0.121, 0.124, 0.087. The test flags 0 to 1.1% of neurons before onset. The script's own measure, the fraction 0.25 s before the cue, is 0.054, 0.125 and 0.383, the last inside the middle-delay photoinhibition.
deviations: Neuron selection from the deposited script (analysis_compile_all_data_unilateral.m, Fig. 1f section), which fills M3's open inclusion rule. The authors' MATLAB scripts deposited in the data set (alm-3/live/analyses_scripts/), which the data description says reproduce the paper's figures, are used as the paper's analysis code for details the claims file and the Methods leave open; the paper itself links no code.

outcomes.statement: After unilateral photoinhibition ALM neurons recover more than 80% of their control selectivity within 514 ms; recovery times are 373 +- 260 ms (sample), 510 +- 218 ms (early delay) and 327 +- 112 ms (window ending 0.3 s before the cue).
outcomes.source: Results, Preparatory activity after unilateral silencing, paragraph 2; Figure 1g
outcomes.quote: ALM neurons recovered > 80% of their selectivity relative to the unperturbed trials within 514 ms after photoinhibition
outcomes.notes: Every reading of M4 and of the selection is run (96): selection rule (the scripts' sample or delay epoch with |preference| > 1, or M3's any epoch), screening trials (the code's 5 per type, 10 per type, 10 in total), preference window (whole count or most selective epoch), trials of the selectivity test, more than 2 or 3 trials per condition, 200 ms windows stamped at their centre or 400 ms at their end. Code reading: 347 ms (sample), 420 ms (early delay), 236 ms (middle delay), within 373 +- 260, 510 +- 218 and 327 +- 112 ms, at least 99% of resamples recovering in each condition. In all 96 readings every condition recovers in at least 96% of resamples, and 34 put all three times within tolerance. No reading gives the paper's 55 neurons: 66 to 160 (72 under the code's reading). Of 292 Experiment 1 pyramidal neurons, 99 are selective in the sample or delay epoch and 72 remain after the preference and trial filters; selection by any epoch leaves 135 to 137. The times match, on a different neuron set, so the neuron count, an expected value, fails.
deviations: Screening, selection and the bootstrap recovery rule from the deposited script (analysis_compile_all_data_unilateral.m, Fig. 1g section): 5 control trials of each type set the preference (the Methods' subset of 10 trials), the recovery time is searched from offset to 1 s after the cue. The authors' MATLAB scripts deposited in the data set (alm-3/live/analyses_scripts/), which the data description says reproduce the paper's figures, are used as the paper's analysis code for details the claims file and the Methods leave open; the paper itself links no code.

Every reading of M4 (screening 10 trials per type or in total; preference from the whole count or the most selective epoch) and the selection of M3 (any epoch) are run alongside the code's; the most selective epoch is the one where the screening trials differ most by mean difference over pooled standard deviation, a standard choice.

A recovery time counts as within tolerance only when at least half the bootstrap resamples recover (the paper does not say how resamples that never recover were counted; see the methods_unavailable finding).
PSTHs are evaluated every 10 ms (the script uses 1 ms), so recovery times are resolved to 10 ms.

outcomes.statement: Neurons whose rates decrease during the delay epoch also recover after unilateral photoinhibition, returning to the time-matched control trajectory and not decaying to the end-point rate.
outcomes.source: Extended Data Fig. 4b, c; Results, Preparatory activity after unilateral silencing, paragraph 2; Figure 1e
outcomes.quote: Spike rate difference relative to time-matched control show significantly smaller root-mean-squared error (RMS) than spike rate difference relative to end point (p<0.001, paired t-test)
outcomes.notes: 55 Experiment 1 pyramidal neurons from 4 mice have a significantly lower rate in the last than in the first 400 ms of the delay (paper 27 from 6 mice). The RMS windows start after photoinhibition has ended and the end point is the control rate in the last 400 ms of the delay. For the 47 tested, 200 ms windows from 0.1 s after offset to 0.1 s before the cue: RMS to the time-matched control 0.462, to the end point 0.429 after early-delay photoinhibition (paired p = 0.27), 0.500 against 0.494 with the three conditions pooled (p = 0.74); 400 ms windows stamped at their end, from 0.4 s after offset to the cue: 0.378 against 0.367 (p = 0.65) and 0.451 against 0.470 (p = 0.52). Experiment 2 (106 neurons, 7 mice): p = 0.92 and 0.43. Neurons with increasing rates: time-matched smaller when pooled (p = 0.041 and 0.049), not after early delay alone (p = 0.086 and 0.28). The round-1 result (time-matched larger, p = 0.019) used windows that overlapped photoinhibition and a different end point; the two changed together, so the effect of the window alone was not isolated.
deviations: The start and end of the delay are read as its first and last 400 ms (criterion). RMS windows: 200 ms stamped at their centre from 0.1 s after offset to 0.1 s before the cue, or 400 ms stamped at their end from 0.4 s after offset to the cue, so that none overlaps photoinhibition or the response epoch.
The paper's 6 mice cannot come from Experiment 1, which has 4 mice in the data set; Experiment 2 is shown as a variant. Asked of a reader (questions/crcns-alm-3.yaml).

outcomes.statement: After transient photoactivation of layer 5 IT neurons, ALM selectivity recovers to 80% of control in 249 +- 68 ms (sample), 275 +- 168 ms (early delay) and 250 +- 218 ms (middle delay).
outcomes.source: Results, Preparatory activity after unilateral silencing, paragraph 2; Extended Data Fig. 5f
outcomes.quote: After photostimulus offset, ALM activity and selectivity recovered with a time-course that was similar to recovery after photoinhibition
outcomes.notes: The photoactivation data (Tlx_PL56-cre x Ai32 mice) are not in the data set; its FAQ says they were not published and would be added. No other public copy was found.

outcomes.statement: Unilateral photoinhibition in the early delay reduces performance only slightly (1 spot 70.3%, 4 spots 67.7%), while bilateral photoinhibition degrades it severely (1 spot per side 58.0%) or to near chance (4 spots per side 51.4%).
outcomes.source: Results, Preparatory activity after bilateral silencing, paragraph 1; Figure 2b
outcomes.quote: Behavioral performance was only slightly affected after unilateral photoinhibition with a single spot during the early delay epoch ( Fig. 2b , 70.3% correct, p = 0.009, two-tailed t-test against control); unilateral photoinhibition with four spots had small additional effect (67.7%, p=0.003). In contrast, using only two spots across both hemispheres caused performance to degrade severely ( Fig. 2b , 58.0%, p<0.001; difference from 4 spot unilateral: p<0.05, two-tailed t-test); four spots bilaterally further reduced performance to near chance level (4 laser spots: 51.4%, p<0.001)

statistics.about: bilateral 1 spot per side against control
bilateral 1 spot per side against unilateral 4 spots
bilateral 4 spots per side against control

outcomes.notes: Bilateral recording sessions, performance pooled per mouse: control 78.0%; unilateral 1 spot 69.3% (10 mice, paired p = 0.025, within 70.3 +- 7.0); unilateral 4 spots 75.6% (3 mice, p = 0.15; paper 67.7%); bilateral 1 spot 65.8% (3 mice, p = 0.045; paper 58.0%); bilateral 4 spots 58.1% (7 mice, p = 0.0001; paper 51.4%). Bilateral 1 spot against unilateral 4 spots 65.8 against 75.6% (3 mice, p = 0.12). The order unilateral, bilateral 1 spot, bilateral 4 spots holds with each below control; three values are outside tolerance and two tests not significant.
deviations: Recording sessions only (0.8 s photoinhibition from delay onset, 10 mice); the paper's values come from 13 mice including behaviour-only sessions with 0.8 and 1.3 s photoinhibition.

outcomes.statement: Bilateral photoinhibition biases movements inconsistently across mice and sessions, and the direction of a session's bias follows which control trajectory its perturbed cd trajectories approach.
outcomes.source: Results, Preparatory activity after bilateral silencing, paragraph 1; Extended Data Fig. 6
outcomes.quote: Bilateral photoinhibition biased movements inconsistently across mice and sessions
outcomes.notes: 16 sessions of fig3-cd-roc. 8 sessions are biased under bilateral photoinhibition (Fisher p < 0.05), 6 toward lick right and 2 toward lick left. The sign of the bias agrees with the nearer control trajectory (reading b) in 7 of 8 (0.88) and with the side of the decision boundary (reading a) in 5 of 8 (0.62). With all units, 0.75 and 0.62. Over all 16 sessions the bias and the mean perturbed projection correlate with Spearman r = 0.34 (p = 0.20).
deviations: The claim is reproduced under reading (b) of the criterion and not under reading (a). The criterion's last sentence judges agreement with the side of the decision boundary, which is reading (a); whether reading (b) may decide is asked of a reader (questions/crcns-alm-3.yaml).

outcomes.statement: Spike rate and selectivity of left ALM neurons recover within 600 ms after ipsilateral photoinhibition, contralateral photoinhibition hardly affects activity, and after bilateral photoinhibition the rate recovers on average but selectivity does not; selectivity recovery takes 538 +- 178 ms (ipsilateral), 192 +- 114 ms (contralateral) and does not occur (bilateral).
outcomes.source: Results, Preparatory activity after bilateral silencing, paragraph 2; Figure 2c-e
outcomes.quote: As before ( Fig. 1 ), spike rate (> 90 %) ( Fig. 2c, d ) and selectivity (> 80%) ( Fig. 2e ) recovered 600 ms after ipsilateral perturbation. ALM activity was hardly affected by contralateral photoinhibition ... After bilateral photoinhibition neurons recovered their spike rate on average ( Fig. 2c, d ), but selectivity failed to recover
outcomes.notes: Experiment 2 (types 4, 5, 6). Rates: ipsilateral 0.958 of control 600 ms after offset (0.963 without the rate exclusion) with 9.4% of neurons significantly changed (both readings recover); contralateral 0.901 during photoinhibition; bilateral 1.114 of control just before the cue (1.134 without the exclusion), outside the criterion's 10%. Selectivity, 64 readings of M4 and the selection: contralateral 240 ms under the code's reading (146 neurons), within 192 +- 114; bilateral reaches 80% before the cue in at most 1% of resamples in every reading. Ipsilateral: 25% of resamples recover under the code's reading (716 ms among them, 854 ms counting the others at the cue); 0% to 79% across readings. Six readings, all with 10 screening trials drawn in total (M4 reading b), have at least half the resamples recovering with both times within tolerance and bilateral not recovering; one (code rule, preference from the most selective epoch) also has 146 neurons, within 143 +- 14.3 (ipsilateral 684 ms from 51% of resamples, contralateral 229 ms). In every reading ipsilateral selectivity 0.2 s before the cue is 28% to 60% below control, and 28% to 43% in those six readings, so where it reaches 80% it falls back before the cue. The ordering holds under those six readings and the bilateral rate misses the criterion, so the claim holds in part, on few readings. The criterion's partial rule names a time outside tolerance; here both times are within tolerance and the bilateral rate fails, so the partial outcome follows the protocol's general meaning (the effect holds only in part), not the criterion's wording.
deviations: Selection, screening (10 trials per type) and the recovery rule (searched from offset to the cue) from the deposited script analysis_compile_all_data_bilateral.m, Fig. 2e section. The authors' MATLAB scripts deposited in the data set (alm-3/live/analyses_scripts/), which the data description says reproduce the paper's figures, are used as the paper's analysis code for details the claims file and the Methods leave open; the paper itself links no code.
Every reading of M4 and of the selection is run, as for fig1g-selectivity-recovery; a recovery time counts only when at least half the resamples recover.

outcomes.statement: Bilateral photoinhibition with one spot per side causes a larger persistent change in selectivity than unilateral photoinhibition with four spots; recovery takes 490 +- 280 ms (ipsilateral 4 spots), 235 +- 156 ms (contralateral 4 spots) and does not occur (bilateral 1 spot).
outcomes.source: Results, Preparatory activity after bilateral silencing, paragraph 2; Extended Data Fig. 7d
outcomes.quote: Bilateral photoinhibition with one laser spot produced a larger persistent change in selectivity than unilateral photoinhibiton with four laser spots
outcomes.notes: Experiment 3 sessions (types 7, 8, 9), 64 readings of M4 and the selection, 29 to 61 neurons (paper 40; 32 under the code's reading). Ipsilateral and contralateral 4-spot times within tolerance in 40 readings (code reading 530 and 119 ms, against 490 +- 280 and 235 +- 156 ms). Bilateral 1-spot selectivity reaches 80% of control before the cue in 36% to 99% of resamples (80% under the code's reading), where the paper reports no recovery; no reading has both the times within tolerance and the bilateral selectivity unrecovered. Delta selectivity in the last 400 ms of the delay: bilateral 1 spot -0.55 against ipsilateral 4 spots -0.21 spikes/s (32 neurons, paired p = 0.53), -0.46 against -0.11 with selection by any epoch (59 neurons, p = 0.27). With the bilateral 1-spot neurons of the sessions with types 4, 5 and 7 pooled (54 to 121 neurons, a variant for a question to a reader), 32% to 77% of resamples recover.
deviations: Method of fig2-bilateral-recovery on the Experiment 3 sessions; the deposited scripts contain none for Experiment 3.

outcomes.statement: Recovery of selectivity after unilateral photoinhibition is less robust with larger photoinhibition, and cd trajectories separate at the end of the delay with ROC 0.80 +- 0.08 (control), 0.64 +- 0.10 (ipsilateral 4 spots), 0.68 +- 0.15 (contralateral 4 spots) and 0.54 (bilateral 1 spot).
outcomes.source: Results, Preparatory activity after bilateral silencing, paragraph 2; Extended Data Fig. 7e
outcomes.quote: Recovery of selectivity after unilateral photoinhibition was less robust with larger photoinhibition size ( Extended Data Fig. 7e ) ... control, 0.80 ± 0.08; ipsilateral, 0.64 ± 0.10; contralateral, 0.68 ± 0.15; bilateral, 0.54 ± 0.8
outcomes.notes: 4 of the 6 Experiment 3 sessions pass the session rule. Mean-difference cd, pyramidal neurons, code split: ROC 0.762 (control), 0.621 (ipsilateral 4 spots), 0.702 (contralateral 4 spots), within tolerance, and 0.604 (bilateral 1 spot), outside 0.54 +- 0.054 and within the 0.08 variant. No reading puts the bilateral value within 0.054 (0.598 to 0.642), and the criterion has no partial rule. Ipsilateral 4 spots 0.621 against Experiment 2 ipsilateral 1 spot 0.706, so recovery is less robust with larger photoinhibition. With the bilateral 1-spot sessions holding types 4, 5 and 7 pooled (9 sessions), the bilateral ROC is 0.570 to 0.602, within 0.054 in 4 of 6 readings; whether the paper pooled them is asked of a reader.
deviations: Four of the six Experiment 3 sessions pass the session rule, each with trials in every group (five with all units); with 4 sessions the s.e.m. of the control ROC is 0.14.

outcomes.statement: Along the coding direction, trajectories for lick right and lick left recover after ipsilateral photoinhibition (ROC at the end of the delay 0.73 +- 0.02 against control 0.76 +- 0.03), are little affected by contralateral photoinhibition (0.74 +- 0.03), and stay collapsed after bilateral photoinhibition (0.58 +- 0.03).
outcomes.source: Results, Robustness along the coding direction, paragraph 2; Figure 3b, c; Extended Data Fig. 8
outcomes.quote: ROC values between trajectories at the end of delay epoch: control, 0.76 ± 0.03; ipsilateral, 0.73 ± 0.02; mean ± s.e.m. across sessions, Methods). Contralateral photoinhibition had little effect ( Extended Data Fig. 8 ; ROC, 0.74 ± 0.03). As expected ( Fig. 2 ), trajectories were permanently altered after bilateral photoinhibition, resulting in small separation between the trajectories for different trial types at the time of movement onset (ROC, 0.58 ± 0.03)
outcomes.notes: The session rule of the deposited script (pyramidal neurons stable at trial 50 and 50 before the end, more than 5 neurons, at least 5 trials per group) gives the paper's 16 sessions from 7 mice (175 neurons). Leave-one-out split (M6 reading b), mean-difference cd, pyramidal neurons: ROC 0.731 +- 0.025 (control), 0.713 +- 0.023 (ipsilateral), 0.742 +- 0.033 (contralateral), 0.592 +- 0.033 (bilateral), all within tolerance; windows centred in the epochs give 0.733, 0.712, 0.749, 0.593. Other readings miss: the code's split gives 0.719 and 0.706 for control and ipsilateral, just below tolerance; random halves give a contralateral 0.684; all units give an ipsilateral 0.667 to 0.681. Control, ipsilateral and contralateral exceed bilateral by more than 0.1 in the matching reading. With more than 5 trials in every group (the Methods' wording) 12 sessions remain and the ROC is 0.681, 0.692, 0.723, 0.554 (code split), the control value outside tolerance.
deviations: cd is the mean difference of the Methods; the deposited script's linear discriminant is shown as a variant with the code's split and random halves (not with leave-one-out).
The reproduced outcome rests on one of the criterion's readings (leave-one-out, pyramidal neurons); the control and ipsilateral values lie near the edge of their tolerance in all readings.
The session rule keeps groups of 5 trials, as the deposited script does, which gives the paper's 16 sessions; M6's "> 5 trials per condition" gives 12 sessions and is shown as a reading.

outcomes.statement: During photoinhibition the cd separation falls (ROC 0.54 +- 0.03 ipsilateral, 0.64 +- 0.03 contralateral, 0.54 +- 0.01 bilateral, against control 0.72 +- 0.02).
outcomes.source: Extended Data Fig. 8 legend
outcomes.quote: ROC values during the time period of photoinhibition: control, 0.72 ± 0.02; ipsilateral, 0.54 ± 0.03; contralateral, 0.64 ± 0.03; bilateral 0.54 ± 0.01
outcomes.notes: Reading (b), projections averaged over the photoinhibition period, with all single units and the code split: ROC 0.703 (control), 0.534 (ipsilateral), 0.642 (contralateral), 0.539 (bilateral), all within tolerance (0.72 +- 0.02, 0.54 +- 0.03, 0.64 +- 0.03, 0.54 +- 0.01). 3 of 32 readings match. With pyramidal neurons the bilateral value is 0.51 and outside its tolerance of 0.01; with window (a) the ipsilateral values are 0.490 to 0.544 and the bilateral values 0.473 to 0.526, and no reading matches.
deviations: The matching reading uses all single units (M6 reading b) and the window average (reading b).

outcomes.statement: The direction of the lick right minus lick left response difference is stable through the sample and delay epochs (correlation between late sample and late delay 0.61 +- 0.05).
outcomes.source: Methods, Analysis of population dynamics in the activity space; Extended Data Fig. 9b
outcomes.quote: During the sample and delay epochs the direction of the difference in the mean response vectors, w t = x̄ lick right – x̄ lick left , was stable (correlation of w t 's between late sample epoch vs. late delay epoch, 0.61 ± 0.05
outcomes.notes: All correct control trials: Pearson correlation of w between the last 400 ms of the sample and of the delay 0.590 +- 0.075 over 16 sessions (pyramidal), 0.622 +- 0.060 over 17 (all units); within 0.61 +- 0.05. With the correct training trials only, 0.520 and 0.570.

outcomes.statement: The projection on cd captures 65.6 +- 5.1% of population selectivity and 36.4 +- 6.3% of task-related activity variance over the sample and delay epochs; modes 1 to 5 together explain 98.5 +- 0.5% of the variance and 95.8 +- 1.2% of the selectivity.
outcomes.source: Methods, Analysis of population dynamics in the activity space; Extended Data Fig. 8a
outcomes.quote: The projection along the cd captured 65.6±5.1% of the population selectivity ... and 36.4±6.3% of the total variance in ALM task-related activity ... Mode 1-5 together explained 98.5±0.5% of the total variance of task-related activity and 95.8±1.2% of population selectivity over the sample and delay epochs
outcomes.notes: Mean-difference cd (Methods), random halves of the control trials (M6 reading a), pyramidal neurons, pre-sample baseline, squared-norm shares (the script's): selectivity on cd 67.1% (paper 65.6 +- 5.1), variance on cd 39.9% (36.4 +- 6.3), both within tolerance; modes 1 to 5 variance 96.3% (98.5 +- 0.5) and selectivity 92.5% (95.8 +- 1.2), outside. No reading puts all four within tolerance. With the code's split the cd selectivity share is 72.5% and with leave-one-out (all control trials) 74.7%, outside; RMS shares give cd values near 81% and 61%, outside, and mode 1 to 5 values near 98% and 96%. With the script's discriminant cd and its split, 66.1% and 36.6%. With modes 2 and 3 and the mean responses from correct trials only (the criterion's trials), pyramidal neurons, random halves: 72.8% and 42.7% on cd, 96.8% and 94.5% for modes 1 to 5; no reading puts all four within tolerance either way.
deviations: Modes, baseline (the window 3.4 to 3.0 s before the cue) and the squared-norm shares from the deposited script (analysis_compile_all_data_bilateral_activityModes.m, ED Fig. 8 sections), with the mean-difference cd of the Methods; the script's discriminant cd is a variant. The modes are fully Gram-Schmidt orthogonalized (Methods); the script orthogonalizes the persistent modes against the singular vectors only. The shares use only training trials, so leave-one-out amounts to using all control trials.

outcomes.statement: Deviations along the coding direction predict the upcoming movement trial by trial, in control trials and after unilateral and bilateral perturbation, even when average selectivity is destroyed.
outcomes.source: Results, Robustness along the coding direction, paragraphs 2 and 4; Figure 3c; Figure 4b; Extended Data Fig. 8b, 9e
outcomes.quote: Individual trials with a deviation toward the “lick right” trajectory along the cd predicted more frequent “lick right” responses and vice versa ( Fig. 4 , Extended Data Figs 6b and 9 ). This analysis shows that even after average selectivity is destroyed by perturbations, ALM population dynamics still dictate upcoming movements
outcomes.notes: Trials pooled over 16 sessions. Prediction accuracy from the side of the boundary: control 0.728 (412 trials, binomial p = 3.2e-21), ipsilateral 0.686 (p = 6.9e-12), contralateral 0.684 (p = 2.4e-12), bilateral 0.671 (p = 1.3e-16); logistic slopes 0.145, 0.138, 0.105, 0.105, p below 2.5e-10. On error trials alone accuracy is 0.53 to 0.67. After bilateral photoinhibition the fraction of lick right responses is 0.33 in the most negative and 0.77 in the most positive projection bin.

outcomes.statement: The persistent mode is altered by perturbation up to and beyond movement onset but neither discriminates trial type nor predicts behaviour; the ramping mode shows non-selective ramping in the delay, is resistant to unilateral and bilateral perturbation and does not predict behaviour.
outcomes.source: Results, Robustness along the coding direction, paragraph 3; Figure 3d, e; Extended Data Fig. 8b-e
outcomes.quote: However, this projection did not discriminate trial type nor predict behavior on control trials. Third, a mode that maximally captured the remaining activity variance, showed non-selective ramping during the delay epoch, did not predict behavior, and was resistant to unilateral and bilateral perturbations
outcomes.notes: Persistent mode (mode 2): control ROC 0.567, prediction accuracy 0.568 (binomial p = 0.003), ipsilateral change -2.09 against a control s.e.m. band of 2.17. Ramping mode (mode 4): control ROC 0.577, accuracy 0.570 (p = 0.002), ipsilateral +0.51 and bilateral -0.48 against a band of 1.00. The ROCs are within 0.5 +- 0.1 and the ramping mode is robust, but both modes predict the lick above chance and the persistent mode's ipsilateral change lies inside its band. With all units the ramping accuracy is 0.529 (p = 0.12) and the persistent accuracy 0.547 (p = 0.026).
deviations: Modes from ed8a-mode-variance with the mean-difference cd; the code's split and random halves are run, the leave-one-out split is not (it needs all modes recomputed for every control trial). With random halves both modes still predict the lick above chance (p = 1e-05 and 0.002).

outcomes.statement: Reaction times are faster on trials whose cd trajectory lies far from the decision boundary at the go cue.
outcomes.source: Extended Data Fig. 9f
outcomes.quote: Reaction times are faster on trials in which the trajectory is far from the decision boundary at the time of the ‘go’ cue
outcomes.notes: The reaction time needs lick times. The data set has no lick events, and its lick trace shows detectable licks in 42 of 90 sessions and in none of the 26 Experiment 2 sessions (trace range 0.0013 to 0.0019 against about 0.05 in sessions with licks; their only channels are lick_trace, aom_input_trace and laser_power). Variants on other sessions with licks, not the claim's sessions: 4 Experiment 3 population sessions, control r = -0.019 (p = 0.84), all conditions r = -0.153 (p = 0.001); 5 sessions with types 4, 5, 7, r = 0.017 (p = 0.86) and 0.029 (p = 0.55); 15 callosotomy sessions, r = -0.025 (p = 0.66) and -0.025 (p = 0.38).

outcomes.statement: Corpus callosum bisection leaves performance unaffected, but makes performance highly sensitive to unilateral photoinhibition, with a significant interaction, dropping to the level of bilateral photoinhibition in control mice.
outcomes.source: Results, Contralateral input is required for recovery, paragraph 1; Figure 5b; Extended Data Fig. 10b
outcomes.quote: Remarkably, behavioral performance was unaffected ( Fig. 5b , control trials, before vs. after callosotomy, p>0.05, two-tailed t-test) ... However, behavioral performance was now highly sensitive to transient unilateral photoinhibition ( Fig 2b , 1 laser spot: p=0.0019, two-tailed t-test against control). There was a significant interaction between callosotomy and unilateral photoinhibition (p=0.0035, repeated measure two-way ANOVA)

statistics.about: control performance before against after callosotomy
unilateral 1 spot against control after callosotomy
interaction of callosotomy and unilateral photoinhibition

outcomes.notes: Only sessions after the cut are in the data set (5 to 6 daily sessions per mouse), so the before-and-after comparison and the interaction cannot be tested. After the cut, ipsilateral 1-spot photoinhibition lowers performance from 74.6% to 59.1% (7 mice, paired p = 0.0033; per-session means 73.9% to 57.9%, p = 0.0071), and 59.1% is within 58.0 +- 5.8%. Control-trial performance of the callosotomy mice and of the control mice (different animals) is shown for context.
deviations: Judged on the after-cut test alone, as the criterion says when no sessions before the cut exist.

outcomes.statement: After callosotomy, ALM neurons recover their average spike rate after ipsilateral photoinhibition but not their selectivity, selectivity recovers after contralateral photoinhibition (217 +- 228 ms) and not after bilateral, and selectivity along cd is reduced.
outcomes.source: Results, Contralateral input is required for recovery, paragraph 2; Figure 5c-f
outcomes.quote: After ipsilateral photoinhibition, ALM neurons recovered their average spike rate ( Fig. 5c, d ), but selectivity failed to recover ( Fig. 5e ). Selectivity in the cd direction was reduced ( Fig. 5f , 16 sessions)
outcomes.notes: Callosotomy sessions (types 10, 11, 12), code reading, 125 neurons (paper 129). Ipsilateral rate 1.053 of control just before the cue (1.081 at 600 ms after offset); ipsilateral selectivity 67% below control 0.2 s before the cue, reaching 80% in 0.3% of resamples. Contralateral 297 +- 251 ms, within 217 +- 228. Bilateral selectivity reaches 80% in 0 of 1000 resamples. The session rule gives 16 callosotomy sessions (Fig. 5f: 16). Ipsilateral cd ROC 0.566 against the callosotomy control 0.718 (paired p = 0.006) and the Experiment 2 ipsilateral ROC 0.706 (p = 0.003). Across 64 readings of M4 and the selection, ipsilateral selectivity reaches 80% in at most 9% of resamples and bilateral in at most 0.2% (one or two of 1000 resamples in seven readings, none in the others), and 37 readings put the contralateral time within tolerance from at least half the resamples.
deviations: Conditions as the data set labels them; selection and recovery rule from the deposited script analysis_compile_all_data_bilateralCCX.m. The authors' MATLAB scripts deposited in the data set (alm-3/live/analyses_scripts/), which the data description says reproduce the paper's figures, are used as the paper's analysis code for details the claims file and the Methods leave open; the paper itself links no code.
Reduced read as lower by a t-test over sessions at p < 0.05, a standard choice.

outcomes.statement: Preparatory activity after callosotomy is similar to that of control mice, with 254 of 496 putative pyramidal neurons selective.
outcomes.source: Results, Contralateral input is required for recovery, paragraph 2; Extended Data Fig. 10e, f
outcomes.quote: Preparatory activity in callosotomized mice (n=7 mice) was similar to control mice ( Fig. 5c ; Extended Data Fig. 10 ), providing additional evidence that the two ALM hemispheres can maintain preparatory activity independently
outcomes.notes: 519 units labelled pyramidal in the callosotomy sessions (paper 496); 521 by the width of the mean waveform, with or without upsampling. Selective: 259 with correct and error trials (within 254 +- 25.4), 303 with correct trials. Fraction 0.499 against 0.642 in control mice under the same reading (0.584 against 0.711 with correct trials), more than 10 points lower. Delay selectivity of selective neurons rises from 1.08 spikes/s 1.5 s before the cue to 2.44 0.1 s before. The selective count and the rising delay selectivity hold; the neuron count and the similarity of fractions fail, and the criterion has no partial rule.

outcomes.statement: Monolithic network models (fixed-point attractor, integrators, trained recurrent networks) do not recover their unperturbed trajectory after transient silencing of half of their neurons.
outcomes.source: Results, Robust model networks, paragraph 1; Figure 1c; Extended Data Fig. 1f-i, 4c
outcomes.quote: Overall, all “monolithic” models consisting of one network were unable to explain robustness
outcomes.notes: Simulated: the simple integrator (three connectivity draws) ends 21% of its selectivity away from the unperturbed output; the single-module attractor switches fixed point (deviation 1.02 to 1.09 of its selectivity) with either neuron silenced; the FORCE-trained networks (three draws, ramp learned with RMS error near 0) end 25% to 87% away. All draws of all three exceed the 20% criterion. Not simulated: the integrator with corrective feedback (ED Fig. 1g), whose weights the paper does not give, and the tamed-chaos network (ED Fig. 1i), whose pruning threshold and retuning it does not give. The criterion has no partial rule; the outcome is partial because two of the five models could not be tested. The simple integrator's deviation (0.212 against the threshold of 0.2) depends on the assumed rank-one matrix.
deviations: The simple integrator's matrix is taken as 0.99 u u^T with random u, the FORCE target as a linear ramp, with output feedback and an RLS update every 2 ms (standard choices; see models.py).
Two of the five model classes could not be simulated for lack of parameters.

outcomes.statement: Modular networks of two coupled modules (attractor, integrator, trained recurrent network) restore activity after transient silencing of one module but drift to a random fixed point when both are silenced.
outcomes.source: Results, Robust model networks, paragraph 2; Figure 6b-d; Methods, Modeling and simulation
outcomes.quote: Selective commissural connections restored activity on the other side after unilateral transient silencing ( Fig. 6b ). When the two sides are silenced, the network drifts to one of the fixed points randomly
outcomes.notes: Modular attractor, noise drawn each step: recovery after unilateral silencing in 100% and 98% of runs (lick right, lick left). After bilateral silencing, 80% and 83% of runs have not settled at 2 s (wrong side in 45% and 63%); run to 4 s every run settles, at the wrong fixed point in 47% and 55%, within 25% to 75%. With noise of the same intensity per unit time the unperturbed attractor already ends at the wrong fixed point in 45% to 49% of runs, so that reading is not a working model. Modular integrator with the printed matrix: after silencing module 1 its selectivity returns to 13.6 against 14.4 on lick right trials, but to -7.2 against -14.4 on lick left trials, as its recovery neuron is driven only by right-preferring activity. The attractor part holds, the integrator part on one trial type; the modular FORCE network was not simulated. The criterion has no partial rule and needs both the attractor and the integrator to recover in at least 90% of runs; the integrator recovers in 50%, so the claim is not reproduced (set in round 3, as the verifier agreed).
deviations: Noise taken as variance 0.01 per integration step (1 ms), the reading under which the attractor holds its choice; the per-unit-time reading is shown.
The inter-module partner of each attractor neuron is taken to share its preference.
Bilateral silencing of the attractor is also run to 4 s, not only to the criterion's 2 s, so that every run settles at a fixed point; the wrong-fixed-point fractions at 4 s are used.

findings.statement: The cell-type labels do not match the paper's classes. In the 58 non-callosotomy sessions 89 units are labelled FS and 33 have no label, where the paper reports 72 FS and 50 excluded units of intermediate width (0.35 to 0.45 ms); 890 pyramidal agree. 15 units labelled FS have a trough-to-peak width of 0.358 ms in their deposited mean waveform, and 24 unlabelled units are narrower than 0.35 ms.
The data description lists a depth field for each unit; the files have none (fields timeUnit, eventTimes, eventTrials, waveforms, channel, cellType), and the waveform field is named waveforms.
Photostimulation type 9 is still described in the files and the data description as "Right ALM (ipsilateral)"; the data set's FAQ says it is contralateral.

The lick trace shows detectable licks in only 42 of 90 sessions with performing trials, and in none of the 26 Experiment 2 sessions, where it is flat (range about 0.002 against 0.05 elsewhere). The files hold no lick event times, so reaction times cannot be measured for the paper's population analyses.

The behaviour-only sessions (Fig. 1d, Fig. 2b, ED Fig. 3), the photoactivation recordings (ED Fig. 5), the recordings in untrained mice (ED Fig. 2d), sessions before callosotomy (Fig. 5b) and the simulations named in the data set's title are not in the data set. The FAQ says the photoactivation data would be added.

In four sessions (ANM257636_20150404, ANM264411_20141224, ANM273657_20150325, ANM298738_20150727) photoinhibition of the left ALM does not reduce pyramidal activity (rate after laser onset 0.71 to 2.18 times the rate before), where every other session drops to a median of 0.03. That spikes, laser trace and trial table share a clock could not be shown for these sessions.

Nothing in the files says which experiment a session belongs to. Six sessions from three mice hold types 4, 5 and 7 (ipsilateral 1 spot, contralateral 1 spot, bilateral 1 spot), a combination the Methods do not describe for either bilateral experiment, and the deposited scripts analyse neither these nor the Experiment 3 sessions.
Session ANM270340_20150618 has no performing trials (GoodTrials is 0 for all 322 trials).

verifications.by: Independent agent run by CatalystNeuro (same harness, separate context, did not write the notebook)
verifications.reviewed: Round 1. The first executed notebook with the conclusion cells and the summary removed, the helper modules and the claims file, with the paper. The verifier checked the archive listing and the FAQ for the blocked claims and tested helper functions on synthetic inputs. Its report had no attempt record and gave its own outcome for each claim; 22 of 29 agree with the record it was given.

disagreements.reason: The population mean is not above control (p = 0.57 and 0.62), but in the first 400 ms 24 neurons are significantly excited against 9 suppressed, and the criterion needs fewer excited than suppressed. The criterion may misread "a low level of sustained inhibition" as per-neuron significance (B13 i).

All three recovery times are within tolerance in all four 200 ms readings and nearly every resample recovers, but the neuron count is 70 to 87 against 55 +- 5.5 in every reading, so this is not the paper's neuron set. Selection uses sample or delay only with a |preference| > 1 filter where M3 says any epoch (B3), and the other M4 readings were not run (B4).

Ipsilateral rate recovers (0.958, 9.4% changed), but ipsilateral selectivity reaches 80% before the cue in only 1 to 30% of resamples, and the deficit at -0.2 s is 0.48 to 0.58 in every reading. The rows flagged within tolerance come from 30% and 16% of resamples (B1). Contralateral and bilateral selectivity agree with the paper. Bilateral rate is 1.114 at the cue, outside 10%.

Bilateral 1 spot reaches 80% of control before the cue in 51 to 80% of resamples (335 to 557 ms), and the claim needs it not to. Neurons 32 or 29 against 40 +- 4. Bilateral delta selectivity is larger than ipsi 4 spots, but p = 0.53.

Bilateral 1-spot ROC is 0.598 to 0.642, above the 0.594 limit, in every reading; it passes only with the 0.08 variant tolerance. Ipsi 4 spots (0.62) is below Exp 2 ipsi 1 spot (0.71). Only 4 or 5 sessions. The ED Fig. 2b n of 102 suggests the bilateral 1-spot sessions with types 4, 5, 7 were pooled (B13 ii).
519 callosotomy pyramidal neurons against 496 (tolerance 0). The selective fraction is 12.7 to 14.3 points below control mice, more than the 10 allowed. The selective count (259) is within tolerance.

The modular integrator does not recover on left trials (-7.2 against -14.4); the printed matrix causes this, and the Fig. 6c gating neurons do not appear in the 8 x 8 matrix. The attractor's step-noise result passes, but the bilateral random fixed point check rests on states that have not settled (B5).

verifications.by: Independent agent run by CatalystNeuro (same harness, separate context, did not write the notebook)
verifications.reviewed: Round 2. The full executed notebook after the round-1 revision, with the conclusions and the summary, the helper modules, the README, the attempt record and the claims file, with the paper. The verifier agreed with 28 of 29 outcomes and disagreed with fig6-modular-models-robust. Its general points (README run time; MD5 sums copied from checksums.md5, not computed from the bytes read) were answered by printing the notebook's run time and computing each file's MD5 from the bytes read and comparing it with checksums.md5 (all 91 match).

disagreements.reason: The record says partially reproduced; it should be not reproduced. The criterion has no partial rule. It needs the integrator to recover in at least 90% of runs, and on lick-left trials it does not (cell 90, -7.2 against -14.4). For ed2e, ed7e and ed10e the record changed the outcome to not reproduced as the criterion has no partial rule; the same rule applies here. An incomplete matrix in the paper belongs in the methods_unavailable finding and does not make the outcome partial. Running bilateral silencing to 4 s, not 2 s, is not listed as a deviation.

verifications.by: Independent agent run by CatalystNeuro (same harness, separate context, did not write the notebook)
verifications.reviewed: Round 3. The one proposed change of outcome, on fig6-modular-models-robust, and the analysis behind it in the re-executed notebook (cells 89 to 91), models.py, the attempt record and the claims file, with the paper. Nothing else was reviewed.

paper_notes.statement: The deposited analysis scripts differ from the Methods. The coding direction is a Fisher discriminant averaged over time (func_discriminant.m), where the Methods define it as the mean difference of the response vectors. The selectivity test uses correct and error trials although its comment says correct trials; the paper's ED Fig. 1 counts (634, 176, 337, 493) are matched by correct trials (633, 176, 336, 493) and not by the script's trials (571, 152, 287, 404). The unilateral script screens 5 trials per type for the preference, the bilateral ones 10, where the Methods say 10 trials. The population session rule of the scripts keeps groups of 5 trials, which gives the paper's 16 sessions, where the Methods say more than 5 trials per condition (12 sessions).

Questions for the authors. (1) Fig. 6b: is the noise variance of 0.01 per integration step, and what step was used? Per unit time the attractor does not hold its choice. (2) Fig. 6c: with the printed matrix the recovery neuron restores only right-preferring activity, so lick left trials do not recover; is the matrix complete? (3) ED Fig. 4: the 27 neurons come from 6 mice, but Experiment 1 has 4 mice in the data set; which sessions and photoinhibition conditions were used? (4) Fig. 2e: how were bootstrap resamples that never reach 80% before the cue counted in the recovery time? In this data set most ipsilateral resamples do not.

ED Fig. 2b, ED Fig. 4 and the Results give 6 mice for Experiment 1, but the 20 unilateral sessions, the paper's count, come from 4 mice in the data set. The ED Fig. 2b neuron counts (117, 110, 109; 300, 294, 301; 52, 52, 102) differ from those here (180; 319 to 323; 56), and its 102 for the Experiment 3 bilateral condition suggests that other bilateral 1-spot sessions were pooled.

entries.name: li-2016-crcns-alm-3
entries.title: Robust preparatory activity in mouse premotor cortex (Li, Daie, Svoboda and Druckmann 2016)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Li, Daie, Svoboda and Druckmann (2016) on CRCNS data set alm-3, which holds the sorted single units, trial tables, photostimulus types and lick and laser traces of 91 recording sessions from 19 mice performing a delayed response task with transient unilateral or bilateral photoinhibition of the anterior lateral motor cortex, with and without callosotomy. It covers unit counts and selectivity, silencing and recovery of rates and selectivity, behaviour in the recording sessions, and the population analyses along the coding direction.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Li et al. (2016) from CRCNS alm-3
